$comment: Static fixture, modelled on tct-007's three-step sequence. `tct_token` is the committed signed example known-answer/signed-examples/tct/kat-keypair-001-issues-002.json (`iss` = kat-keypair-001, `sub` = `aud` = kat-keypair-002), as in tct-022, and `tct_token_claims` is its `decoded_claims`. A runner MUST NOT re-mint it. `self_aid` is the token's `iss`: the verifier is the issuer, receiving its own TCT back (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5). The reference clock `__NOW__` = 1711900000 applies, and at it the TCT is fresh. The input carries no `expected_audience`: under §10.5 the verifier takes the expected audience only from the authenticated presenter AID, never from the token. `issuer_policy.pop_posture: enforce-for-all` is the deployment posture that requires downstream PoP for every grant (RFC-AITP-0005 §6). `pop_required_grants` lists every grant in the token, so a runner that configures PoP only through the per-grant surface of §6.2 sets the same posture. Only the envelope signature is a placeholder, minted with the sender key (kat-keypair-002). scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs and scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py both check that the token is the signed example and verifies, that `self_aid` is its `iss`, and that the input carries no `expected_audience`.
description: A genuine TCT is presented back to its issuer to invoke a capability, with no `pop_response` (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5, §6.2). The verifier is the token's `iss`, the token's `aud` = `sub` names the presenter, and the deployment requires PoP for every grant. Under §10.5 the issuer establishes the presenter's AID only from downstream PoP or a channel binding to the `sub` key, and this fixture has no channel binding. The verifier MUST issue a `pop_challenge` and, when no `pop_response` arrives, MUST reject the invocation with POP_RESPONSE_INVALID. A verifier that authorizes the invocation on the token alone, for example by checking `aud` against `sub` in the token, accepts a bearer token and fails this fixture.

expected.rationale: The issuer accepts the invocation request for processing. It has not authorized it: under the enforce-for-all posture it MUST first challenge the presenter.
The issuer MUST issue a `pop_challenge` for the token's `jti`: PoP is the only source of the presenter's AID in this fixture (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5 item 3).

No `pop_response` arrives, so the issuer has no authenticated presenter AID to compare with `sub` and `aud`. It MUST reject with POP_RESPONSE_INVALID and MUST NOT authorize the capability (RFC-AITP-0005 §10.5 items 3 and 4).
